title: Persistence: Supabase and the Showmob API
summary: How Showmob can move from repository JSON and browser-local drafts to secure revisions, media storage and an API without losing portability.

blocks.title: Add memory without trapping the artifact
blocks.body: Right now every Showmob page is a JSON file in the repo, and Studio drafts live in your browser. Supabase can give Showmob durable revisions, identities, permissions and media. The JSON artifact remains the portable language; the database records who may change it, how it evolved and which revision is live.

blocks.title: This is the implementation plan, not a live-data claim
blocks.body: Today, canonical pages still come from repository JSON and Studio drafts stay in browser storage. No Supabase project, schema, authentication flow or API endpoint is introduced by this page.

blocks.heading: Words before wiring
rows: Postgres
The database Supabase runs for you. It stores rows in tables, like a spreadsheet with strict rules.
JSONB
Postgres's way of storing a whole JSON document inside one row. The complete artifact sits in a single cell and the database can still search inside it.
RLS (row level security)
Rules on a table that decide which rows each person may see or change. Two people can query the same table and get different rows.
Grants
The permissions underneath RLS that say which operations - read, add, change, delete - a role may use on a table at all.
Publishable key
A key that is safe to ship in the browser. It can only do what the grants and row rules allow.
Secret and service-role keys
Master keys that skip the row rules entirely. They stay on the server and must never reach the browser.
Data API
Supabase's built-in way to read and write tables over HTTP. Useful plumbing, but not the product's public promise.
Edge Function
A small piece of server code Supabase runs for you on request. Vercel Functions do the same job on Vercel.
Idempotency key
A label on a request that means: if this arrives twice, only do it once.
blocks.caption: Every term the rest of this page uses, explained before it shows up.

nodes.title: Request
nodes.detail: A person or authorized agent submits an artifact change.

nodes.title: Authorize
nodes.detail: The API checks who is asking and what they are allowed to do.

nodes.title: Validate
nodes.detail: The same Showmob runtime contract rejects malformed content.

nodes.title: Revise
nodes.detail: One transaction stores an immutable revision and advances the current pointer.

nodes.title: Render
nodes.detail: The app reads the selected revision and uses the existing renderer.

blocks.heading: Give each Supabase service a narrow job
rows: Postgres
Artifacts, immutable revisions, series membership, permissions and audit facts
Artifact JSON stays versioned and exportable
Auth
Stable user identity and sessions
Who may do what comes from ownership and membership rows, not user-editable metadata
Storage
Draft and published media objects
Private by default; type, size, ownership and lifecycle are enforced
Data API
Narrow browser reads or draft operations
Only deliberately exposed tables, with grants and row rules on; plumbing, not the public Showmob contract
Edge or Vercel Functions
Publication, agent writes, validation and multi-record workflows
Master keys stay server-side and never reach the browser
Realtime
Optional collaboration signals after core persistence works
Presence is not a substitute for durable revision history
blocks.caption: Adopt only the services a proven workflow needs. Persistence comes before collaboration effects.

blocks.heading: Separate the artifact from its operating envelope

columns.name: Portable document
columns.detail: The complete schema-versioned Showmob JSON: metadata, theme, series and blocks. It can be exported, reviewed in Git and rendered without Supabase.

columns.name: Persistence envelope
columns.detail: Database IDs, owners, memberships, revisions, audit timestamps, media records and publication state. It makes collaboration safe without leaking into the content language.

blocks.title: Exposure is now an explicit decision
blocks.body: On current Supabase projects, a new table is not automatically reachable through the Data API. Showmob must choose which schema is exposed, grant only the operations it needs and turn on row rules for every exposed table, instead of assuming a table is reachable.

blocks.heading: Security gates before the first hosted write

items.label: Row rules on every exposed table
items.detail: Each person can read or change only the rows they own or belong to, checked on both reads and writes.

items.label: Least-privilege grants
items.detail: No role can read, add, change or delete an object unless the product actually needs that operation.

items.label: Publishable key only in the browser
items.detail: Secret and service-role keys stay in protected server environments because they skip the row rules.

items.label: Private draft media
items.detail: Storage rules bind uploads and reads to the correct owner, project and bucket; public media is a deliberate publication step.

items.label: Immutable revision evidence
items.detail: Every accepted change records who submitted it, when, and which validated document became current.

items.label: Agent writes reviewed like user writes
items.detail: An agent receives scoped authority, never a blanket bypass, and proposed publication remains reviewable.

items.title: Keep GitHub canonical
items.detail: Finish the artifact language and keep the current renderer dependable.

items.title: Prove the round trip
items.detail: Write one validated artifact revision to Supabase, read it back and check that what comes back matches the exported JSON exactly.

items.title: Add identity and drafts
items.detail: Introduce Auth, ownership and membership rules, then persist private drafts without changing publication.

items.title: Add media
items.detail: Upload constrained files to private Storage and attach reviewed asset records to artifact revisions.

items.title: Open the Showmob API
items.detail: Move publication and authorized agent workflows behind versioned endpoints with validation, audit evidence and retry-safe requests.

items.title: Move reads deliberately
items.detail: Serve hosted artifacts from persistence only after parity, rollback and production observability are proven.

blocks.heading: The API grows around product rules

slides.title: Direct where it is truly simple
slides.body: An owner-scoped draft read can use Supabase's Data API when grants and row rules fully express the rule.

slides.title: Server-side where actions have meaning
slides.body: Publish, archive, accept an agent proposal and advance a revision pointer are product operations. Put them behind Showmob endpoints.

slides.title: Version the public promise
slides.body: Clients should depend on artifact and workflow semantics, not table names. The database can evolve behind the API.

slides.title: Make retries safe
slides.body: Networks retry. Each write request carries an idempotency key - an only-do-this-once label - so a retry cannot create duplicate revisions or duplicate uploads.

blocks.heading: Prove one revision before moving the product
blocks.body: The next implementation should create a Supabase development project, write the smallest secure schema, validate one artifact into an immutable revision, read it back and run the existing renderer and contract tests against the result.
